name: Neural Tube Closure Defect

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in Hispanic and Caucasian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Neural Tube Defects

criteria.description: Presence of an open or closed defect in the neural tube confirmed by imaging or surgical findings
Associated cranial abnormalities such as Arnold-Chiari malformation or hydrocephalus
Neurological impairments consistent with level and severity of defect (e.g., lower limb weakness, sensory loss)
Prenatal ultrasound evidence of neural tube defect such as lemon sign or banana sign

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a neural tube defect by imaging or surgical confirmation with or without neurological deficits
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Prenatal diagnosis is possible via ultrasound and maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein screening.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Open spinal dysraphism with exposed neural tissue
searchTerms: open spinal defect with exposed nerves
spinal opening with visible neural tissue

pathognomonic.symptomName: Meningocele presenting as a cystic spinal mass

pathognomonic.notes: Fatal defect characterized by absence of major portions of the brain and skull

common.symptomName: Lower limb motor weakness or paralysis
Hydrocephalus due to impaired cerebrospinal fluid flow

common.notes: Neurogenic bladder and bowel are common sequelae

common.symptomName: Orthopedic deformities including clubfoot and hip dislocation

searchTerms: brain tissue herniation at skull base

occasional.symptomName: Skin dimples or hairy patches overlying closed defects
searchTerms: skin dimples or hairy patches over spine
small skin indentations or hair tufts on back

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory difficulties due to brainstem involvement
searchTerms: respiratory difficulty due to brain damage

rare.symptomName: Tethered cord syndrome with progressive neurological deterioration
searchTerms: tethered spinal cord with worsening symptoms
spinal cord stuck causing neurological decline
progressive nerve problems from tethered cord

rare.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata such as hemangiomas or lipomas overlying defect
searchTerms: skin marks like hemangiomas over defects
birthmarks or fatty lumps on spine

laboratory: Elevated maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) during pregnancy
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing lemon sign, banana sign, or direct visualization of defect
MRI demonstrating spinal cord abnormalities and associated brain malformations
CT scan for bony defects in the skull or spine
genetic: No single gene mutation; multifactorial inheritance with genetic and environmental factors
Variants in folate metabolism genes (e.g., MTHFR) may increase risk
other: Folic acid deficiency as a major modifiable risk factor
Amniocentesis showing elevated AFP and acetylcholinesterase

distinguishingFeatures: Closed spinal defect without exposed neural tissue
Usually asymptomatic or mild neurological signs
Herniation of brain tissue through skull defect
Distinct from open neural tube defects involving spinal cord
Abnormal development of lower spine and sacrum
Associated with maternal diabetes, differs in embryological origin

redFlags: Open spinal defect with exposed neural tissue at birth
Severe lower limb paralysis or sensory loss
Signs of infection or CSF leakage from defect
